tunnels.title: Tunely
tunnels.intro: Klientský koniec tunela beží tu, kde sa obsluhujú účty. Serverový koniec beží na relé, ku ktorému sa pripájajú používatelia a ktoré sem presmeruje svoje porty. Druhý koniec vytvorte párovacím kódom alebo pridajte relé a nechajte ho nastaviť tento panel.
tunnels.introEdition: Tento server je relé: používatelia sa pripájajú k nemu a ich porty idú cez každý tunel na panel, ktorý ich obsluhuje. Importujte tunel párovacím kódom z toho panela alebo mu v Nastaveniach dajte API token s rozsahom tunnel, aby tunely nastavoval sám.
tunnels.importHint: Vložte kód, ktorý druhý panel zobrazuje pre tento tunel. Koniec toho istého páru sa nahradí, takže novší kód ho aktualizuje.
tunnels.pairingHintClient: Importujte tento kód na stránke Tunely na relé, aby sa vytvoril jeho koniec. Adresa nižšie je, ako relé dosiahne tento server.
tunnels.pairingHintServer: Importujte tento kód na paneli, ktorý obsluhuje účty, aby sa vytvoril jeho koniec. Adresa nižšie je, ako ten panel dosiahne toto relé.
tunnels.relaysHint: Relé je ďalší Manifold, zvyčajne edícia Tunnel Server. Na ňom v Nastavenia → Zabezpečenie vytvorte API token s rozsahom tunnel a sem zadajte URL jeho panela a ten token. Tento panel potom vytvára, aktualizuje a odstraňuje koniec relé pri každom tuneli.
tunnels.deleteRelayConfirm: Zabudnúť toto relé? Jeho tunely zostanú na oboch serveroch a už sa nebudú synchronizovať.
tunnels.resyncHint: Znova pošle každý tunel na jeho relé s aktuálnou adresou servera. Použite po presune panela na iný server.
tunnels.resyncDone: Každé relé má znova svoje tunely
tunnels.name: Názov
tunnels.kindHint: Linky jadra sú rýchle a bez šifrovania; GRE prenáša IPv4 aj IPv6, SIT IPv6, IPIP IPv4. Tunely BackPack prejdú filtrovanými trasami: reverzný vytáča klientsky koniec, L3 je šifrovaný link.
tunnels.roleHint: Klient: panel, ktorý obsluhuje účty. Server: relé, ku ktorému sa pripájajú používatelia a ktoré presmeruje porty klientovi.
tunnels.relayHint: S relé tento panel vytvorí a aktualizuje druhý koniec sám.
tunnels.transportHint: Ako cestujú spojenia reverzného tunela. tcpmux a wssmux sa hodia pre väčšinu filtrovaných trás; kcp a quic potrebujú UDP; pck a xdi raw sokety.
tunnels.carrierHint: Ako cestujú pakety L3 tunela: udp a quic na otvorenej trase, pck a sni ako TCP, xdi v pingu.
tunnels.dialerHint: Druhá strana počúva na porte tunela. Ak sa pripája klient, relé nepotrebuje jeho adresu a panel sa môže presunúť bez zásahu do relé.
tunnels.remoteAddrHint: Link jadra potrebuje verejnú IP druhého servera. Klientsky koniec BackPack prijme aj názov hostiteľa relé.
tunnels.localAddrHint: Viaže link na jednu z adries servera. Prázdne nechá voľbu na trase, čo je správne, ak má server jednu.
tunnels.publicAddrHint: Ako druhý server dosiahne tento; zapíše sa do jeho konca. Prázdne použije zistenú verejnú IP.
tunnels.portHint: Kde počúvajúca strana čaká na druhú. Musí byť otvorený vo firewalle toho servera.
tunnels.tokenHint: Oba konce majú rovnaké tajomstvo; nesie ho párovací kód.
tunnels.localIpHint: Adresa s prefixom, napríklad 10.80.0.2/30; druhý koniec použije inú v ňom.
tunnels.mtuHint: Prázdne nechá miesto na vonkajšie hlavičky pri trase 1500 bajtov. Znížte, keď sa veľké prenosy zasekávajú.
tunnels.greKeyHint: Rozlíši viac GRE linkov medzi tými istými servermi. Oba konce majú rovnaký kľúč.
tunnels.natHint: Maskarádovanie funguje vždy, no všetci používatelia vyzerajú, že prichádzajú z relé. Zachovať — panel vidí adresu každého, ktorú potrebuje limit zariadení a záznam IP; odpovede idú späť tunelom.
tunnels.proxyProtocolHint: Odovzdá adresu používateľa službe za tunelom. Zapnite, len ak každý presmerovaný inbound prijíma PROXY protocol.
tunnels.forwardsHint: Relé počúva na týchto portoch a posiela ich tunelom na port klientskeho konca. Konfigurácie ukazujú na relé, takže panel sa môže presunúť bez ich zmeny.
tunnels.kernelServerHint: Otvorte presmerované porty vo firewalle tohto relé. Link jadra nešifruje; spojenia používateľov zostávajú šifrované od konca po koniec.
tunnels.deleteConfirm: Odstrániť tunel? Používatelia cezeň budú odpojení.

groups.title: Groups of origins
groups.intro: Join this relay's tunnels to several origin servers under shared ports. Failover sends everything to the first origin that answers and moves to the next within seconds when it stops; balance spreads new connections over every origin that answers.
groups.name: Name
groups.failoverHint: The members are tried in the order listed; the first that answers its probe takes every connection.
groups.balanceHint: Each new connection goes to the next member that answers; a connection stays on its member until it ends.
groups.membersHint: Relay ends of kernel or layer-3 tunnels, one to each origin. Green marks where the ports go now.
groups.confirmDelete: Delete this group? Its ports stop being forwarded.

suspendedNotice.volume: Your traffic allowance is used up: your users are switched off until the next cycle or until it is raised.

access.accountExpiryHint: When the reseller's account ends: its users are switched off and it can no longer sign in. Empty never.
access.actsAsHint: The account whose access the token gets; it never reaches further than that account.
access.adminsIntro: Everyone who signs in to the panel: main admins, operators and resellers. A reseller sees and manages only the users it created, inside the allowance set here.
access.basedOnHint: The tier decides which part of the panel the role reaches at all; the role can only narrow it.
access.brandingHint: What this reseller's customers see in their apps and on their subscription page, in place of the panel's own.
access.changeLoggingOff: Change logging is off, so only sign-ins and exports are recorded.
access.changeOwnerHint: Hand {count} users to another account. Their past traffic stays charged to whoever owned them.
access.clearLogConfirm: Delete every audit entry? This cannot be undone.
access.deleteAdminConfirm: Delete this account? Its users pass to the panel and keep working; its API tokens are deleted.
access.deletePlanConfirm: Delete this plan? Users created from it keep their limits.
access.endSessionsConfirm: End every login of this account?
access.handoverConfirm: Make {name} the panel's owner? Only the new owner can hand the panel on after that.
access.inboundsLimitedHint: On: this reseller's users are put only on the allowed inbounds, and so reach only their servers.
access.limitsHint: Ceilings over what accounts on this role may hand out; 0 means no limit. The tighter of the role's and the account's own value holds.
access.mayEditUsersHint: Off: it can create users but not change or remove them afterwards.
access.name: Name
access.noRestriction: No restriction: every permission of the tier
access.plansIntro: Presets users are created from: a volume, a length, limits and inbounds. A plan is copied onto the user once; editing it later changes no existing user.
access.plansOnlyHint: On: every user it creates must come from one of the allowed plans, with the plan's limits.
access.renewEveryDaysHint: Renews the expiry and resets usage every N days; 0 never.
access.rolesIntro: A role narrows one tier: the permissions it keeps and limits on what its accounts may hand out. It can never reach beyond its tier.
access.startOnFirstUseHint: Count the length from the user's first connection instead of from creation.
access.tierHint: Main admins reach everything; operators run the panel but not its administration; resellers reach only their own users.
access.volumeHint: Traffic all of this reseller's users may use per cycle; 0 is unlimited.
access.subDomainHint: Links of this reseller's users are built on it; *.domain gives each user a host of its own. It needs a DNS record pointing here.

ingress.intro: One TCP port, such as 443, for many services. Each connection goes to the target its TLS server name (SNI) or HTTP host names, unchanged, so REALITY and TLS inbounds, the panel and the subscription server can all answer on 443. Move each of them to a free local port, such as 127.0.0.1:8443, and point a route at it. Runs on this server only.
ingress.listenHint: An IP of this server; empty listens on all of them.
ingress.routesHint: Tried from the top; the first whose host (and ALPN, if set) fits takes the connection.
ingress.hostsHint: Names or addresses; *.example.com matches one label under it. For REALITY, the server name the inbound pretends to be.
ingress.targetHint: host:port the connection is handed to, usually an inbound or the panel moved to 127.0.0.1.
ingress.proxyProtocolHint: Tells the target the client's real address. Turn on acceptProxyProtocol in that inbound's transport, or the device limit and IP log see 127.0.0.1.
ingress.alpnHint: Optional: only TLS clients offering one of these, such as h2.
ingress.defaultTargetHint: Where a connection no route names goes, such as a web site to show scanners. Empty closes it.
ingress.confirmDelete: Delete this shared port and free it?

backups.intro: Full backups on a schedule, to this server, an S3-compatible bucket (AWS, Cloudflare R2, ArvanCloud, MinIO) or another server over SSH. With a passphrase each backup is sealed (AES-256-GCM) and restore asks for it. Only the newest backups a target keeps are left there; other files are never touched. Restore under Overview → Backup.
backups.name: Name
backups.everyHoursHint: Hours between backups; 0 backs up only when you press Run now.
backups.keepHint: How many of the newest backups stay there; 0 keeps them all.
backups.dirHint: Empty uses /etc/manifold/backups. A second disk or a mounted share keeps them apart from the panel.
backups.endpointHint: The S3 address without the bucket, such as https://s3.amazonaws.com or your R2 / ArvanCloud address. Buckets are addressed path-style.
backups.passphraseHint: Seals every backup to this target. Without it nobody, the panel included, can restore them: keep it somewhere else.
backups.passphraseAdvice: A full backup holds every user, key and certificate. Set a passphrase before sending it off this server.
backups.secretKept: Set. Leave empty to keep it.
backups.confirmDelete: Delete this target? Backups already stored there stay.
backups.sealedHint: This backup is sealed. Enter the passphrase of the target that made it.

webhooks.intro: Events are sent out as they happen: users created, changed, disabled, expiring, out of traffic or connecting for the first time; nodes going down or hitting their usage limit; backups; the panel's health. Send them to your own bot (signed JSON), an ntfy topic for push notifications, or a Bale chat. A failed delivery is retried for about a day.
webhooks.urlHint: Receives a POST with the event as JSON. Check X-Manifold-Signature: sha256=HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + body), with the timestamp from X-Manifold-Timestamp.
webhooks.urlInvalid: Enter an http:// or https:// address
webhooks.ntfyHint: The ntfy.sh topic or your own ntfy server, such as https://ntfy.sh/my-panel. Subscribe to the same topic in the ntfy app.
webhooks.chatIdHint: The Bale chat, group or channel the bot posts to; the bot must be a member.
webhooks.secretGenerated: Leave empty and one is made for you, shown once.
webhooks.eventsHint: Leave empty for every event, including ones added later.
webhooks.testQueued: Test sent; see the delivery log for the answer
webhooks.secretOnceHint: Copy it into your bot now; the panel will not show it again.
webhooks.confirmDelete: Delete this webhook and its delivery log?

certs.intro: Certificates the panel gets from Let's Encrypt and renews by itself, or ones you upload. Inbounds and the panel read them from the files shown; pick one in an inbound's TLS settings with "From the certificate store". A wildcard (*.example.com) needs DNS-01 with a Cloudflare or ArvanCloud token.
certs.name: Name
certs.nameHint: The folder the files are kept in, /etc/manifold/certs/<name>/.
certs.domainsHint: Type each and press Enter. *.example.com covers every subdomain but not example.com itself; add both if you need both.
certs.badDomain: One of these is not a domain name
certs.wildcardDns: A wildcard can only be proved with DNS-01

challengeHint.dns-01: The panel writes a TXT record through your DNS provider's API. Works behind a CDN, for wildcards, and without any free port.
challengeHint.http-01: The domain must point at this server with port 80 free while the order runs (stop nginx or another web server first). Not behind a CDN proxy.
challengeHint.tls-alpn-01: The domain must point at this server with port 443 free while the order runs, which usually means Xray is not on 443.

tokenHint.cloudflare: A Cloudflare API token with Zone → DNS → Edit on the zone (My Profile → API Tokens).
tokenHint.arvancloud: An ArvanCloud API key (Profile → Machine user / API keys), with or without its "Apikey" prefix.

certs.portHint: Empty for the standard port. Another one only helps when something forwards the standard port to it.
certs.emailHint: Optional; Let's Encrypt writes to it about problems with the account.
certs.stagingHint: Let's Encrypt staging: no rate limits, but browsers do not trust what it issues. For trying a setup out.
certs.nodesHint: Each renewal is copied to these nodes, to the same path, so their inbounds read it too.
certs.confirmDelete: Delete this certificate and its files on this server?

import.intro: Bring users over from Marzban, PasarGuard, Marzneshin, 3x-ui, x-ui, s-ui, Hiddify or Remnawave. Each keeps its UUID or password, quota, usage, expiry and reset cycle, and its old subscription link keeps working here.
import.drop: Drop the old panel's database or backup here
import.dropHint: SQLite database (.db, .sqlite3) or a Hiddify backup (.json); the kind is recognised by itself.
import.whereFiles: Marzban: /var/lib/marzban/db.sqlite3 · PasarGuard: /var/lib/pasarguard/db.sqlite3 · Marzneshin: /var/lib/marzneshin/db.sqlite3 · 3x-ui/x-ui: /etc/x-ui/x-ui.db · s-ui: /usr/local/s-ui/db/s-ui.db · Hiddify: Settings → Backup. A Marzban or PasarGuard on MySQL is read over the API instead.
import.urlHint: Where its dashboard opens, with the port, without the /dashboard part.
import.secretHint: Optional. The secret_key of the old panel's jwt table; with it every link it ever handed out keeps working, without it only each user's current link does. MySQL: SELECT secret_key FROM jwt;
import.whereTo: Which inbounds each protocol's users go to
import.fallbackHint: Inbounds for users who have no credential for any protocol picked above; they get new ones.
import.keepLinks: Keep the old subscription links working
import.keepLinksHint: Point the old subscription domain at this server and give the subscription server the old path (Settings → Subscription; /sub/ for Marzban, PasarGuard, Marzneshin, 3x-ui and s-ui, the user path for Hiddify, the sub path for Remnawave). Clients then update from the links they already have.
